title: Segal product decomposition of fixed-arity operation spaces
statement:
Use the infinity-category and universe conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid] and the ordinary and generalized nonsymmetric infinity operads of [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability]. Let $Q\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ be a small generalized nonsymmetric infinity operad such that $Q_{[0]}$ and $Q_{[1]}$ are spaces. For an object $C\in Q_{[k]}$, let $\operatorname{Op}_Q(C)$ have as objects active arrows $a:D\to C$ and as morphisms coherent triangles with fixed target $C$ whose source-change edge is an equivalence over an identity of $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$; include all higher simplices. Here active means that the opposite order map preserves the two endpoints. For $1\leq i\leq k$ choose inert cocartesian arrows $C\to C_i$ over $\rho_i:[k]\to[1]$, where $\rho_i^{\mathrm{op}}$ includes $\{i-1,i\}$. Compose $a$ with these arrows and take its inert-active factorization by restricting $D$ to the block between $\alpha^{\mathrm{op}}(i-1)$ and $\alpha^{\mathrm{op}}(i)$, where $\alpha$ is the base map of $a$. This defines a natural equivalence of spaces
$$\operatorname{Op}_Q(C)\simeq\prod_{i=1}^k\operatorname{Op}_Q(C_i).$$
The equivalence is compatible with inert-preserving maps of such generalized operads and their images of $C$. For $k=0$ the product is a point, so $\operatorname{Op}_Q(C)$ is contractible. For $k\geq1$ this is an equivalence on the union of all input arities; an operation on the left of input arity $n$ corresponds to operations on the right with input arities $n_1,\ldots,n_k$ satisfying $n_1+\cdots+n_k=n$. No source-change morphism is permitted to change an input arity.

source.place: Erratum proof of Corollary E.0.1, product decomposition under inert projections, together with Definitions 2.4.1 and 3.1.13 (generalized Segal and mapping-space conditions) Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-operadic result.

proof.text: Use the generalized Segal equivalence and incidence-diagram axiom stated in [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability]. Since both $Q_{[0]}$ and $Q_{[1]}$ are spaces, its iterated fiber products show that every $Q_{[n]}$ is a space: an inverse to an edge is obtained componentwise, with the same vertex identifications inverted. Thus every source change over an identity is invertible, as required in the definition of $\operatorname{Op}_Q(C)$. Such a triangle has the same source arity and the same base arrow at both ends. Consequently the operation space is the disjoint union of its parts indexed by the active base arrows $\alpha:[n]\to[k]$. This assertion is about the coherent groupoids themselves, with higher simplices retained, rather than their sets of components.

source.place: Definitions 2.4.1(ii), 3.1.13(ii); Erratum, paragraph preceding Corollary E.0.1 (source changes lie over identities).

proof.text: Fix $k\geq1$ and an active base arrow $\alpha:[n]\to[k]$. Put $t_j=\alpha^{\mathrm{op}}(j)$ and $n_i=t_i-t_{i-1}$. Then $0=t_0\leq\cdots\leq t_k=n$. Let $\sigma_i:[n]\to[n_i]$ be the inert arrow whose opposite includes the interval $[t_{i-1},t_i]$, and let $\beta_i:[n_i]\to[1]$ be active. Direct evaluation at $0,1$ gives $\rho_i\alpha=\beta_i\sigma_i$. For $a:D\to C$ choose a cocartesian lift $D\to D_i$ of $\sigma_i$. The mapping-square characterization in [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion], taken over the base factorization $\beta_i\sigma_i$, identifies maps $D_i\to C_i$ over $\beta_i$ with maps $D\to C_i$ over $\rho_i\alpha$. Hence $D\xrightarrow{a}C\to C_i$ factors as a contractibly determined $b_i:D_i\to C_i$. This gives the asserted restriction map $R:\operatorname{Op}_Q(C)\to\prod_i\operatorname{Op}_Q(C_i)$, including its action on coherent triangles and higher simplices: it is induced by these mapping-space equivalences, not by independent choices on points. The required inert lifts exist by [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability].

source.place: Definitions 2.4.1(i), 3.1.13(i); inert block factorization in the product assertion of the proof of E.0.1. Cocartesian factorization is HTT Proposition 2.4.4.3, opposite dual.

proof.text: For $k=0$, an active $[n]\to[0]$ would have to send the sole vertex of $[0]$ simultaneously to $0$ and $n$ in $[n]$, so $n=0$ and the base arrow is the identity. Thus $\operatorname{Op}_Q(C)$ is the space of arrows $D\to C$ in the space $Q_{[0]}$. In the path-space convention of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] this is the space of paths with fixed final endpoint and varying initial endpoint. It contracts to the constant path at $C$: shorten a path by moving its initial endpoint towards its fixed final endpoint. Equivalently its coherent arrow groupoid has terminal object $\mathrm{id}_C$, with the triangle from $a:D\to C$ to $\mathrm{id}_C$ supplied by $a$ itself and its identity homotopy. The possible triangle witnesses form the path space ending at the specified $a$, so are contractible too. This proves exactly the empty-product clause; it does not assert that $Q_{[0]}$ itself is contractible.

source.place: Proof of E.0.1, product assertion at the empty tuple; explicit endpoint/path contraction.

proof.text: To compute a homotopy fiber of $R$ for $k\geq1$, fix a tuple $b_i:D_i\to C_i$, with input arities $n_i\geq0$. Write $V_j\in Q_{[0]}$ for the $j$th vertex projection of $C$, $0\leq j\leq k$. The endpoint projections of $C_i$ are identified with $V_{i-1},V_i$ by the chosen inert projection diagram. Project $b_i$ to each of these vertices and factor through the corresponding endpoint projection of $D_i$. By [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] each factorization has contractible choice. This gives maps $u_i^-:s(D_i)\to V_{i-1}$ and $u_i^+:t(D_i)\to V_i$ in $Q_{[0]}$, together with their composition homotopies. Here $s(D_i),t(D_i)$ denote the first and last vertex; if $n_i=0$ they are the same object. All these maps are equivalences because $Q_{[0]}$ is a space. The endpoint identifications and inert projections used here are precisely those of [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability], including projections to $[0]$.

source.place: Definition 3.1.13, the inert incidence diagram to [0] and [1]; expansion of the sentence using the space assumption on the zero fiber in E.0.1.

proof.text: At the junction of blocks $i$ and $i+1$, glue their endpoint objects by an equivalence $e_i:t(D_i)\to s(D_{i+1})$ and a homotopy $u_{i+1}^-e_i\simeq u_i^+$. The space of such data is contractible: it is the homotopy fiber at $u_i^+$ of postcomposition by the equivalence $u_{i+1}^-$. An inverse to this postcomposition map is postcomposition by an inverse of $u_{i+1}^-$; the associative and unital composition homotopies of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] verify the two inverse equations. Hence postcomposition by $u_{i+1}^-$ is a weak homotopy equivalence, and [lem-coef-spaces-homotopy-fiber-detection], applied with both $u$ and $r$ equal to this postcomposition map and with $q=v$ the identity of its target, shows that each of its homotopy fibers is equivalent to a homotopy fiber of the identity, hence contractible. This also specifies all higher identifications, rather than choosing an equality of vertices. Put $n=\sum_i n_i$. Regroup the source Segal equivalence of [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability] into these blocks: both $Q_{[n]}$ and $Q_{[n_1]}\times_{Q_{[0]}}\cdots\times_{Q_{[0]}}Q_{[n_k]}$ are the limit of the same diagram of $n$ unit edges and their $n+1$ vertices. A zero-length block contributes just its vertex and identity identifications, so contributes no extra edge. A cone on either diagram is the same list of edges and vertex identifications; restricting and concatenating these lists are inverse, also on coherent families. Therefore the glued blocks lift, with contractible space of choices, to $D\in Q_{[n]}$ with its inert block restrictions identified with the specified $D_i$. The junction homotopies ensure that the two descriptions of the map from each shared vertex to $V_i$ agree coherently.

source.place: Definitions 2.4.1(ii) and 3.1.13(ii), regrouped Segal equivalence; explicit endpoint gluing behind the E.0.1 product assertion.

proof.text: Let $\alpha:[n]\to[k]$ be the active map with $\alpha^{\mathrm{op}}(j)=n_1+\cdots+n_j$. For $D$ from step 5, take the block maps $b_i$, and the vertex maps induced by the endpoint factorizations of step 4 and the junction homotopies of step 5. These are exactly a compatible block-and-vertex datum for [lem-coef-operadic-block-incidence-lifting]. Its comparison identifies maps $D\to C$ over $\alpha$ with the homotopy limit retaining these endpoint compatibilities. The fiber over our specified datum is therefore contractible; it supplies $a:D\to C$ with its incidence identifications. This invocation uses the whole incidence diagram, including its vertex objects, and includes zero-length blocks.

source.place: Definitions 2.4.1(iii), 3.1.13(iii); expansion of the incidence/mapping-space part of the product assertion in the proof of E.0.1.

proof.text: Let $L(b)$ be the coherent lifting space of [lem-coef-operadic-operation-lifting-fiber] for the fixed tuple $b=(b_i)$. The endpoint factorizations in step 4, junctions and source lift in step 5, and incidence lift in step 6 are precisely its successive data. The cited comparison gives $L(b)\simeq\operatorname{hofib}_b(R)$ on the full spaces, and is compatible with parameter simplices. In particular it supplies the restriction/extension identification of the full homotopy fiber, including coherent triangles and higher homotopies, without replacing the groupoids by their components. Its hypotheses hold: $Q$ is small and $Q_{[0]},Q_{[1]}$ are spaces, and the source changes lie over identities.

source.place: Definitions 2.4.1(iii), 3.1.13(iii); expansion of the incidence/mapping-space part of the product assertion in the proof of E.0.1.

proof.text: Forget in reverse order the incidence lift, source lift, junction data, and endpoint factorizations in $L(b)$. At each stage the homotopy fiber over every fixed remaining datum is the contractible choice space established in steps 4-6. For each forgetful map $p:A\to B$, apply [lem-coef-spaces-homotopy-fiber-detection] with $u=r=p$ and $q=v=\operatorname{id}_B$: the two fibers are contractible, hence their comparison is an equivalence. Thus $p$ is an equivalence. The finite composite of these maps identifies $L(b)$ with the point of empty lifting data, so step 7 shows $\operatorname{hofib}_b(R)$ is contractible. All fibers here are homotopy fibers; no fibration hypothesis is used.

source.place: Definitions 2.4.1(iii), 3.1.13(iii); expansion of the incidence/mapping-space part of the product assertion in the proof of E.0.1.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-spaces-homotopy-fiber-detection] to $u=R:E\to B$, where $E=\operatorname{Op}_Q(C)$ and $B=\prod_i\operatorname{Op}_Q(C_i)$, with $r=R$, $q=\mathrm{id}_B$ and $v=\mathrm{id}_B$. The maps on fibers compare the contractible fibers just computed with the contractible fibers of $\mathrm{id}_B$, so are equivalences. All objects here are spaces by step 1 and the definition of the operation groupoids, and all are small in the stipulated universe. The node requires no Kan-fibration hypothesis on $R$, since its fibers are homotopy fibers. Thus $R$ is an equivalence. If $B$ is empty there are no fibers to test and the same criterion applies; the constructed map to the empty space forces $E$ empty.

source.place: Proof of E.0.1, product assertion; homotopy-fiber test for the constructed restriction map.

proof.text: The base calculation in step 2 gives $n_i=t_i-t_{i-1}$ and $\sum_i n_i=t_k-t_0=n$. Conversely any tuple of nonnegative arities defines the unique active base arrow by the partial sums used in step 6. Thus the equivalence is on all arities, with exactly the stated sum grading; zero-length blocks have been retained throughout, and no triangle over a base identity changes the arity. For an inert-preserving map $f:Q\to Q'$, use the images of the chosen inert projections as those of $f(C)$ and $f(D)$. Applying $f$ to $D\to D_i\xrightarrow{b_i}C_i$ gives the defining factorization for the restriction of $f(a)$. The cocartesian mapping-space equivalences of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] identify its factor with $f(b_i)$, together with the contractible factorization homotopies and their higher compatibilities. These are comparisons of coherent mapping-space maps, so apply on all parameter simplices and on composites of $f$. Hence $R_{Q',f(C)}\operatorname{Op}_f$ is naturally equivalent to $(\prod_i\operatorname{Op}_f)R_{Q,C}$. Changing any chosen inert lifts gives the same comparison by their cocartesian universal properties. This proves the required naturality of the equivalence, and step 3 supplies it for $k=0$.

source.place: Definitions 2.4.2 and 3.1.17; naturality of the inert product comparison in the proof of E.0.1; explicit arity calculation.
